app.name: Klaviyo OAuth app (developer-owned, for use with Composio)

verdict.summary: Creating and connecting your own Klaviyo OAuth app is quick and needs no review. Composio cannot broker Klaviyo OAuth, so you must register your own app. Public Marketplace listing adds a manual review with several forms and listing assets, and Klaviyo documents no review timeline.
verdict.hands_on_effort: Gate 1 setup: under 1 hour. Gate 3 (Marketplace) preparation and submission: not documented by Klaviyo; plan for multiple working sessions.
verdict.time_to_first_connection: Under 30 minutes once you have an owner, admin, or manager role on the Klaviyo account.
verdict.approval_wait: Not documented. No Klaviyo page read states a review timeline. Unreviewed apps can still be installed through the installation URL while review is pending.

gates.name: Own account (create app and connect your own Klaviyo account)
gates.unlocks: You can create the app, set scopes and redirect URLs, and connect your own Klaviyo account through the authorization flow.
limits: Only owner, admin, and manager roles can create OAuth apps; a regular team member cannot.
Composio's managed OAuth is not available for Klaviyo, so this app is required.
gates.time_to_reach: Minutes, after you have an owner, admin, or manager role on the account.

gates.name: Unreviewed installs through the installation URL (no formal Klaviyo name for this tier)
gates.unlocks: Your app can be installed by customers before it is listed, using the OAuth installation URL. Gathering the five real installs needed for Marketplace submission happens at this gate.
limits: Until Klaviyo approves the app, users see an OAuth warning that the app has not been reviewed by Klaviyo; installs still work.
Install caps or user limits for unreviewed apps are not documented.
Each installed app instance gets its own rate-limit quota (per account per app); the documented example is Create Events at XL (3500/m).
Access tokens last about 1 hour; refresh tokens are revoked if unused for 90 days.
gates.time_to_reach: Immediately after Gate 1. Time to collect five real customer installs is not documented.

gates.name: Marketplace listing (App Marketplace review)
gates.unlocks: Your app can be listed on the Klaviyo App Marketplace, where it is discoverable and loses the unreviewed-app warning.
limits: Requires at least five real customer installs with live API activity; test and developer accounts do not count.
Submission includes company details, app listing information, and the registration and security forms. The security form is required for each app.
Klaviyo may decline the listing for any reason and may require corrections before final approval.
Rejections come with written reasons and can be resubmitted after fixes.
gates.time_to_reach: Not documented. No review timeline appears in the pages read.

steps.title: Confirm you have an eligible role on the Klaviyo account
steps.detail: Check that your Klaviyo user holds the owner, admin, or manager role. Users with other roles cannot create OAuth apps, so ask an owner, admin, or manager to create the app if needed.
gotchas: A regular team member cannot create an OAuth app even with access to the account.

steps.title: Create the app from Manage apps
steps.detail: In Klaviyo, go to Integrations > Developers > Manage apps. Click Create app, enter an app name, and continue. The confirmation screen shows the client ID and client secret.
gotchas: Record the client secret on the confirmation screen; treat it as private.

steps.title: Draft the scope list from the endpoints you actually call
steps.detail: Using the endpoints your integration calls, list only the scopes those endpoints need, and keep accounts:read in the list. Do not copy Composio's default scope list, which is broad and read/write across most resources; unused scopes are a rejection reason.
gotchas: Check each endpoint's reference page to confirm which scope it needs.
Remove any scope the app does not call before saving.

steps.title: Enter the scopes and the Composio redirect URI in the app's OAuth settings
steps.detail: Open the app from Manage apps and go to its OAuth settings. Enter the scope list from the previous step and add the redirect URL. Klaviyo matches the redirect URI character for character, so paste it exactly without changing case, trailing slashes, or protocol.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

values.label: Scopes
values.value: Narrowed list from the previous step; accounts:read included

gotchas: Multiple redirect URLs can be entered separated by spaces, tabs, or new lines.
Whether Composio's callback can be allowlisted on a developer-owned Klaviyo app was not tested. If Klaviyo rejects it, use your own callback URL instead.

steps.title: Save the OAuth settings
steps.detail: Click Save in the top right of the app settings. Re-open the page to confirm the scopes and redirect URLs persisted.

steps.title: Store the client ID and secret in a secrets manager
steps.detail: Save the client ID and client secret in your secrets store, not in application code or a shared document. Plan a rotation schedule.
gotchas: Regenerating the client secret breaks every existing connection that still uses the old secret. Coordinate any rotation with users of the app.

steps.title: Build the PKCE authorization flow and run a test connection
steps.detail: Build the installation URL on the authorize endpoint with response_type, client_id, redirect_uri, scope, state, code_challenge_method=S256, and code_challenge. Generate a new code_verifier (43-128 characters) and code_challenge for every request. Open the URL, log in to your own Klaviyo account, and approve the scopes. Complete the code exchange on your server.
gotchas: Send the token exchange server-to-server with the client secret; never in the browser.
Use a.klaviyo.com for token requests. Requests through www.klaviyo.com are blocked for OAuth token and revoke traffic.
The authorization code expires 5 minutes after issue; restart the flow if an install stalls.

steps.title: Handle token lifetimes and refresh
steps.detail: Store the access and refresh tokens per Klaviyo account. Read expires_in from each token response instead of hardcoding a lifetime, and refresh before expiry. Reject expired tokens in your own code.

values.label: Access token lifetime
values.value: About 1 hour (subject to change; use expires_in)

values.label: Refresh token
values.value: Valid until uninstall; revoked if unused for 90 days

gotchas: Tokens belong to a Klaviyo account, not to an individual user.
A refresh token that sits unused for 90 days is revoked; the account must reinstall.

steps.title: Share the installation URL with five or more real customers
steps.detail: Share the OAuth installation URL with real customer accounts that will generate live API traffic. The app does not need to be listed to be shared. Confirm each install shows Production-level API activity before counting it toward the five required for submission.

values.label: Installs needed
values.value: At least 5 real customer accounts with live API activity

steps.est_time: Not documented; depends on customer outreach
gotchas: Test accounts do not count.
Installs on developer accounts or accounts linked to your company do not count.
Users see a Klaviyo OAuth warning that the app has not been reviewed until it is approved. Installs still work.

steps.title: Add 403 scope-error handling for users who installed before a scope change
steps.detail: Changes to scopes on an existing app reach new installs immediately, but existing installs keep the old scopes until the user reauthorizes. Detect 403 scope errors and prompt those users to reconnect with the new scopes.
gotchas: Marketplace-published apps update scopes without a new review, but existing users still need to reauthorize.

steps.title: Prepare the review package
steps.detail: Draft the app listing content, the testing instructions, and the scope justification. Produce a 48x48 SVG logo with no scripts, four to eight gallery images, and links to your Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, and at least one user guide article. Write the testing instructions from Klaviyo's testing template in a Google Doc with Commenter access.

values.label: Testing doc
values.value: Copy of Klaviyo testing template, Google Doc, Commenter access

gotchas: Links to public documentation are not accepted as testing instructions.
Your app must demonstrate a complete install and uninstall flow, including error handling, and installs must work from both klaviyo.com and its subdomains.
Flows that force avoidable manual steps, or that only start on your own platform, are rejected.

steps.title: Complete the company registration and security forms
steps.detail: Complete the company registration form once for your company. Complete a separate security form for this app. Give Klaviyo's review team test access by adding its review contact to a test account or sending a password reset; never send credentials by email.
gotchas: Omitting either form gets the app rejected.
Do not share account credentials with Klaviyo in the submission or by email.

steps.title: Submit for review from Manage apps
steps.detail: Go to Integrations > Developers > Manage apps, open your app, and click Review submission. Complete the four parts: authentication confirmation, company details, app listing information, and the registration and security forms.

values.label: Menu path
values.value: Integrations > Developers > Manage apps > [app] > Review submission

gotchas: Confirm your app meets the five-install requirement before submitting.

steps.title: Wait for Klaviyo review and respond to feedback
steps.detail: Klaviyo reviews the technical, security, and listing materials. It may require corrections before final approval. Rejections come with written reasons; fix them and resubmit. Klaviyo may decline to list an app for any reason.
gotchas: Keep your app's error rates low; high error rates can lead to delisting.
Logs must be retained for at least 365 days in a tamper-evident store.

requirements.item: Owner, admin, or manager role to create the app
requirements.detail: Only these roles can create OAuth apps in Klaviyo.
The redirect_uri in each authorization request must match an allowlist entry character for character. Paste the Composio callback URL exactly.
Use S256 with a new code_verifier (43-128 characters) and code_challenge for every request.
The client secret stays on the server. Token and revoke calls must go to a.klaviyo.com, not www.klaviyo.com.
The authorization code expires 5 minutes after issue.
accounts:read is added by default and must stay. Every other scope must match an endpoint the app calls.
Use expires_in. Access tokens last about 1 hour. Refresh tokens are revoked after 90 days unused. Expired tokens must be rejected by the app.
Keep OAuth client credentials in a secrets store and rotate them regularly. Regenerating the secret breaks existing connections.

requirements.item: Five real customer installs before submission
requirements.detail: Installs must be real customer accounts with live API activity. Developer and company-linked accounts do not count.

requirements.item: Company registration form and per-app security form
requirements.detail: The company form is completed once per company. The security form is completed for each app. Omitting either gets the app rejected.
SVG logo 48x48 with no scripts, four to eight gallery images, Terms of Service and Privacy Policy links, customer-support contact, and at least one user guide article.

requirements.item: Complete install and uninstall flow with error handling
requirements.detail: Installs must work from klaviyo.com and its subdomains. Flows that need avoidable manual steps are rejected.
Klaviyo may require modifications before final approval; failing to make them can lead to removal from the Marketplace.
Logs retained at least 365 days in a tamper-evident store. Critical or high library vulnerabilities fixed within 3 and 7 days.

scopes.effect: Added automatically and must remain in the list. Tier is not labelled in the pages read.

scopes.scope: All other scopes (for example campaigns:write, profiles:write)
scopes.effect: Each scope must match an endpoint your app calls. Extra scopes are a rejection reason in review. No sensitive or restricted tier was found; least-privilege checking appears to happen within the standard review (inferred).
New installs get new scopes immediately. Existing installs keep old scopes until the user reauthorizes; watch for 403 errors. Marketplace apps update scopes without resubmission.

blockers.symptom: Authorization is rejected or the callback fails because the redirect URI does not match.
blockers.cause: Klaviyo matches redirect URIs exactly against the app's allowlist, and whether Composio's callback is accepted on a developer-owned app was not tested.
blockers.fix: Paste the exact Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page) into the app's redirect URLs and click Save. If Klaviyo still rejects it, you may need to use a callback URL you control and point Composio at it; confirm with Klaviyo support.

blockers.symptom: Submission is rejected for requesting more scopes than the app uses.
blockers.cause: Klaviyo checks requested scopes against the endpoints the app calls, and rejects apps with unused scopes. Composio's default list is broad.
blockers.fix: Narrow the scope list to the endpoints in use, keep accounts:read, remove the rest, and resubmit.

blockers.symptom: Submission is rejected for missing forms or unusable test access.
blockers.cause: Both the company registration form and a per-app security form are required, and reviewers need working test access without credentials sent by email.
blockers.fix: Complete both forms, add Klaviyo's review contact to a test account or send a password reset, and resubmit.

blockers.symptom: Klaviyo's authorize endpoint did not return an OAuth error for an invalid client ID during testing.
blockers.cause: The probe returned a login redirect, so client ID validation behaviour could not be confirmed.
blockers.fix: Do not rely on the probe. Test with your real client ID and confirm the full authorization and token exchange work end to end before onboarding customers.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth for Klaviyo, so you must register your own Klaviyo OAuth app and enter its client ID and secret in Composio. Do not copy Composio's default scope list (read and write across most resources); Klaviyo rejects scopes the app does not use, so narrow the list to the endpoints you call. Composio's callback URL must be added to the app's redirect allowlist exactly as shown in your Composio auth config, and whether Klaviyo accepts that callback on a developer-owned app was not tested. Authorize URL: https://www.klaviyo.com/oauth/authorize. Token URL: https://a.klaviyo.com/oauth/token.

open_questions: No Klaviyo page read states a review timeline in days or weeks.
No install cap or user limit for unreviewed or unlisted OAuth apps was found. The only documented per-app limit is the per-install rate-limit quota.
No sensitive, restricted, or privileged scope tier was found. The scope review appears to be least-privilege checking, but that is an inference.
Whether a free Klaviyo account is enough to create an app, or whether a paid plan is required, was not stated.
Business and domain verification requirements were not found; only company details and a contact email are documented.
Redirect URI rules beyond exact match (HTTP vs HTTPS, localhost, wildcards) were not found.
Whether Composio's callback URL can be allowlisted on a developer-owned Klaviyo app was not tested.
The authorize endpoint did not return an OAuth error for an invalid client_id in the probe, so client ID validation is unconfirmed.
The Composio default scope list was not checked against Klaviyo's endpoint reference pages; the list in this guide is a suggestion to narrow, not a verified set.
